FeetFinder Login

There is one sign-in for buyers and sellers. Most lockouts are a typo, a lookalike page, or a password that lives on a different email than you think.

Dark-Ero editorialUpdated 2026-11-1018+

At a glance

Buyers and sellers sign in on the same official page with an email or username and a password.

There is no official phone app, so a store listing that asks for the password is the fake.

Support is the published address hello@feetfinder.com, and they do not need your password.

Key takeaways

  • Type the address yourself or use a bookmark you saved, and ignore links in random messages.
  • Try the username if the email fails, then a private window, then a password reset.
  • New sellers create the login, pick a plan, and then pass an ID plus a selfie holding it.
  • Basic keeps 85 percent of a sale and Premium keeps 90 percent.
  • Sign out on a shared computer, and do not hand the login to a manager or a buyer.

FeetFinder uses one sign-in for everyone, so there is no separate seller portal to hunt for. You enter the email or the username on the account, then the password.

The click-by-click version, including the reset, is in FeetFinder login. What matters here is knowing which page is real before you type anything.

Fees, buyers and what sellers keep are in our FeetFinder review. A login problem and a pricing question are different errands.

How sign-in works

Type the site address yourself, or open a bookmark you created while you were sure of the page. Links in texts and social posts are how copycat pages collect passwords.

The same email or username works whether you are buying or selling. If you are a seller who also wants to browse, you still use that one page.

On a phone, use the site in Safari or Chrome. There is no FeetFinder download, and a store app that asks you to log in is collecting the password.

The same test, for any adult login, is in how to tell a real adult site from a malware trap. A domain that merely contains the brand, with some other ending, is the one to close.

When the page says no

Check the email spelling first, and remember that passwords are case sensitive. If the email fails, try the username, then refresh, then a private window.

Clear the cookies for the real site, or switch browser, before you assume the account is gone. The reset from the sign-in page is the fastest fix, and it only works for the email that is actually on the account.

Look in spam if the reset mail is missing, and pick a password you do not use for banking or for that inbox. A password manager will also refuse to fill the password on a lookalike host.

If none of that works, email hello@feetfinder.com with the username and a short note on what the page does. A screenshot of the message on screen helps, and the password does not.

Keeping the login

The account holds your files, your buyer messages and your earnings, so the password gets the same care as a bank login. Use a long one, sign out on shared machines, and do not share it with a manager, a friend or a buyer.

Ignore any message that asks you to confirm the password through a link. If you think someone else is in, reset immediately and then tell support.

Leaving the account entirely is a different job from a reset, and the steps are in our how to delete a FeetFinder account guide. Do the reset first if you still want the username.

The source delete note is how to delete your FeetFinder account. A stranger who offers to close or unlock the account for you should never receive the password.

New accounts and the ID check

A new seller creates the login with an email, a username and a password, then picks a plan and completes the identity check. Choose a username you can keep, because buyers will know you by it.

Basic is $4.99 a month and Premium is $14.99 a month, with yearly and lifetime options that cost less if you stay. Sellers keep 85 percent of each sale on Basic and 90 percent on Premium.

The check is a government ID and a selfie in which you hold that ID. Use ordinary light, keep the whole card in frame, and sign up from where you actually are, because a VPN used to dodge a location or age check breaks the terms.

What to write under that new username is in our FeetFinder bio ideas piece. You still have to sound like your own gallery.

The outside examples are in FeetFinder bio ideas. Rewrite them before you paste anything.

Scams around logins are common on every adult shop. The pattern list is how to sell feet pics without getting scammed.

The fee comparison on the ranking site is the FeetFinder review. Read it before you pick Basic or Premium.

If FeetFinder is only one option, the shelf is feet marketplaces. Sign in on the real page either way.

Verdict

Use the official sign-in, the email on the account, and a password you do not reuse. There is no app, and support will not ask you to hand the password over.

Reset before you panic, and write to hello@feetfinder.com when the reset is not enough. Adults only, and a lookalike page is the risk that matters most.

FAQ

Where do buyers and sellers sign in?

On the same official sign-in page, with the email or username on the account and the password. There is no separate seller portal.

Is there a FeetFinder app?

No official phone app exists, so use the website in your mobile browser. Avoid any store listing that asks for the FeetFinder password.

How do I reset a FeetFinder password?

Use the forgot-password step on the official sign-in page and open the link sent to the account email. Check spam, and choose a password you do not use anywhere else.

What if the email will not work?

Try the username, a private window, and a different browser before you contact support. Then email hello@feetfinder.com with the username and what you see on screen.

What does the seller ID check ask for?

A government photo ID and a selfie in which you hold that ID, with the face and the text both readable. A buyer who asks you to send that ID to them is not the check.

Does support need my password?

No, the published support address is hello@feetfinder.com and a real reply will not ask for the password. Anyone who wants it is not support.
